why: Each island is one connected component of '1' cells under 4-directional adjacency; scanning the grid and flood-filling every unvisited land cell counts the components.
hints: Scan the grid. When you hit a land cell you have not seen, you have found a new island. How do you make sure you never count the rest of that island again?
Flood fill: from that cell, BFS/DFS to every 4-connected land cell and mark them visited. The number of flood fills started is the answer.
Visited matrix (the rows are strings, so you cannot overwrite in place unless you copy to lists) plus an explicit stack or queue. O(rows * cols).
pitfalls: Diagonal neighbours do not connect islands.
Recursive DFS on a 300x300 all-land grid overflows Python's recursion limit; use an explicit stack.
Rows are immutable strings: mark visited in a separate structure or convert to lists.
